newsitem.title: GERMANY: German think-tank urges steady interest rates.
newsitem.headline: German think-tank urges steady interest rates.

text.p: The Rhineland-Westphalia Institute of Economic Research (RWI), one of Germany's leading economic think-tanks, said the Bundesbank should keep interest rates steady this year even if U.S. rates move higher.

Ullrich Heilemann, vice-president of the Essen-based institute, told Reuters Financial Television: "The Bundesbank would be well-advised not to follow an American increase... Given the German labour market situation, I don't think there is a policy need here to follow American developments."

Heilemann also said that the Bundesbank should not seek to influence the mark's exchange rate against the dollar. "The Bundesbank should let the dollar go wherever it is going, it should not try to fix a certain exchange rate." he said.

The RWI expects real gross domestic product to grow by 2.5 percent this year, in line with government forecasts. This would not be enough to significantly improve the situation in the labour market, said Heilemann.
"The growth we envisage is too low to absorb the increases in productivity," Heilemann said. He expects an average number of unemployed of 4.1 million in 1997.

Heilemann also said that Germany will not meet the fiscal criteria for monetary union this year. Under the Maastricht Treaty, a country's deficit must not exceed three percent of GDP while overall debt levels should be no higher than 60 percent of GDP.

"We didn't meet them last year and I don't think we will meet them this year -- nevertheless, I believe that EMU will start on time because all participants will agree that Germany is still a source of stability in Europe."
The RWI takes part in the twice yearly economic reports to the government compiled by Germany's six leading institutes for economic research.
